To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The use of a single-agent regimen of etoposide (E) plus cisplatin (P) (EP) for small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is associated with a high rate of response, but a short duration of response and a high rate of relapse, and that the addition of the new agents, ifosfamide (I), vindesine (V), and VP-16, to EP has no impact on survival.

surgery is a safe and potentially curative treatment option for patients with limited-stage small-cell lung cancer (SCLC), and that surgery may be a viable treatment option for patients presenting with extensive-stage SCLC.
the overall survival rate of patients with small cell lung cancer is poor and surgery has a role in the management of this disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the role of surgery in the management of patients with small cell lung cancer (SCLC).
the study of the effects of surgery on the natural course of SCLC, with a view to improving the survival rate of this disease.
the development and application of new methods for the treatment of small cell lung cancers (SCLC) using surgery, radiation therapy, and chemotherapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no data to indicate that surgical management of patients with small cell lung cancer improves their survival and therefore should not be considered.
surgery is not a curative treatment for SCLC and is not recommended in patients with stage IV disease, but that surgery may play a role in selected patients with limited disease.
surgery is a useful modality in the treatment of small cell lung carcinoma.

the results of the present study show that the use of a combination of 5-ALA and PDT is a feasible and effective treatment for the removal of superficial basal cell carcinomas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current standard of care is not sufficient for patients with small cell lung cancer (SCLC).
, in patients with limited-stage small cell lung cancer who have a good performance status, a combination of cisplatin and etoposide is a very effective treatment regimen.

, while there are many different approaches to treating small cell lung cancer, the best results come from combining chemotherapy and radiation therapy, with surgery reserved for patients with early stage disease.
